correctness.rationale: Inductively choose p_i ≡1 mod4 larger than twice the previous square scale, using two new distinct auxiliary splitting primes ell_ij,m_ij ≡1 mod4 for each prior p_j. Hensel gives unit roots of -p_j² modulo each auxiliary prime square; CRT joins them with p_i≡1 mod4 and Dirichlet supplies arbitrarily large primes in that coprime progression. Hence every cross sum p_i²+p_j² has two distinct 1 mod4 squared prime divisors, forcing r_2≥36 by Jacobi; a deleted unordered positive distinct pair accounts for at most eight. Diagonal 2p_i² has r_2=12 while its diagonal pair accounts for four. Growth p_i²>2p_(i-1)² makes distinct unordered deleted-root pairs have distinct sums; an alternative representation cannot have both roots deleted. Every finite prefix preserves the full set S+S. Independently verified finite tuple {5,37,89} for all sums ≤15842; no finite test establishes the Dirichlet construction.
residual_risks: No effective prime-growth bounds; only existence, not arbitrary prime-set deletions.
